{{Short description|Italian astroparticle physicist}}
{{Use dmy dates|cs1-dates=ly|date=July 2022}}
{{Use list-defined references|date=July 2022}}
'''Fiorenza Donato'''  is an Italian theoretical astroparticle physicist whose research involves the study of [[cosmic ray]]s and their use in understanding the nature of [[dark matter]], the possible products of particle collisions involving dark matter, the creation and behavior of [[antimatter]] among high-energy cosmic particles, and [[gamma-ray astronomy]]. She is a full professor of theoretical physics at the [[University of Turin]].{{r|ast}}

==Education and career==
Donato  graduated [[magna cum laude]] from the University of Turin in 1995, and continued at the university for a Ph.D. in physics, completed in 1998. She earned a French [[habilitation]] in 2002, and an Italian professorial habilitation in 2013.{{r|unito}}

She was a postdoctoral researcher at the [[Laboratoire d'Annecy-le-Vieux de physique des particules]] from 1998 to 2001, at the University of Turin from 2002 to 2004, and as an [[Humboldt Fellow|Alexander von Humboldt Fellow]] at the [[Max Planck Institute for Physics]] from 2004 to 2005.{{r|ast}}

She continued as a researcher at the University of Turin, becoming an associate professor there in 2015 and full professor in 2021.{{r|ast}}

==Recognition==
Donato was elected as a [[Fellow of the American Physical Society]] (APS) in 2015, after a nomination from the APS Division of Astrophysics, "for extensive ground breaking contributions in astro particle physics and indirect dark matter searches".{{r|faps}} She became a corresponding member of the {{ill|Accademia delle Scienze di Torino|it}} in 2021.{{r|ast}}
